title: OSWorld2
domain: Long-horizon, real-world tasks on an Ubuntu desktop, across its apps, each in a VM of its own.
good_to_know: Partial credit: each task scores 0 to 1; the score is the mean.
limitations: Not the paper's M3 setup: another release, no residential proxy, and 100 steps with thinking off by default; Steps per task 500 and Thinking adaptive restore the budget.
Muse Spark's published score came from newer upstream code: scores here do not compare with it.
The LLM grader (21 tasks) and the simulated user (6) are Claude Sonnet 4.6: the run's provider must serve it.
29 tasks use the public internet: their outcome can change with the live sites.
Tasks 103 and 104 are not supported: they stay in the datasets, and an agent's unit ends in an error.
A slow or loaded machine, or a run across 16:00 UTC (the VM's midnight), can change scores.
The null control scores above 0 on 015, 076, 090 and 092, and on 077 in some runs.
Only OSWorld-V2's own M3 and Muse Spark run it; no agent from the Agents page yet.
Fetch the gated tasks and prepare the machine first: see OSWorld2 machine setup in the docs.
todo: agent.computer/v1's kit, and the driver's agent side: the upstream's DesktopEnv served to any agent.
The upstream's other agents, beside M3 and Muse Spark.

datasets.title: OSWorld-V2, release osworld-v2.1
datasets.verifier: Each task's own evaluate() on the VM's final state, 0 to 1.

access.step: Ask for access to the gated datasets on Hugging Face
Download the task classes into the upstream's evaluation_examples/task_class
Download the assets into the upstream's cache/osworld_v2_assets
Fetch the VM image into the upstream's docker_vm_data
access.note: osworld-v2-ubuntu-x86.qcow2 from xlangai/v2-image at 6e16459a, about 15 GB unpacked

access.step: Build the proxy image for the 8 tasks that ask for a proxy
access.note: python3 proxy.py --build, from this benchmark's folder
